# odoo-work-cli clock edit

## NAME

odoo-work-cli-clock-edit - Edit an attendance record's check-in/check-out time

## SYNOPSIS

```text
odoo-work-cli clock edit [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--id ID] [--in TIME] [--out TIME] [--json | --format FORMAT]
odoo-work-cli clock edit --create-only [--date YYYY-MM-DD] --in TIME --out TIME [--json | --format FORMAT]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Edit the check-in and/or check-out time of an attendance record.

By default the record of the given day (--date, default today) is edited.
If the day has several records, select one with --id. If the day has no
record yet, one is created when both --in and --out are given. The old and
the new values are printed. Use 'clock list' to see the existing records first.

With --create-only the command only ever creates: if the day already has a
record it aborts with a "conflict" error and changes nothing. Use it when
backfilling days, so that an existing record is never overwritten.

Times are HH:MM on --date or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM". A time more than one
minute in the future, or a check-out not after the check-in, is a
validation error. --id with a record of another day is not_found.

Editing attendance over the API requires the 'Attendance Officer' access
right, with you set as your own attendance manager.

## OPTIONS

`--create-only`
:   Only create; abort with a conflict error if the day already has a record.

    *flag; optional*

`--date` *YYYY-MM-DD*
:   Day of the record to edit, YYYY-MM-DD.

    *string; optional; default: today*

`--id` *ID*
:   ID of the attendance record (required if the day has several records).

    *integer; optional*

`--in` *TIME*
:   New check-in TIME, HH:MM or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM".

    *string; optional*

`--out` *TIME*
:   New check-out TIME, HH:MM or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM".

    *string; optional*

## GLOBAL OPTIONS

`--format` *FORMAT*
:   Output FORMAT: table, json or jsonl.

    *one of table, json, jsonl; optional; default: table*

`--json`
:   Shorthand for --format json.

    *flag; optional*

`--backend` *BACKEND*
:   BACKEND: odoo or fake (offline, made-up data; env ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND).

    *string; optional; default: odoo; env: ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND*

`--config` *FILE*
:   Read only the config FILE (skip discovery).

    *string; optional*

`-h`, `--help`
:   Print the help of the command and exit.

## OUTPUT

"Updated attendance #ID" with the old (was) and the new (now) check-in,
check-out and duration; or "Created attendance #ID: FROM - TO".

With --json the record as it is now plus before, the record before the
edit (null when it was created).

Fields of attendance_edit.schema.json:

`id`
:   *integer*

`employee_id`
:   *integer or null*

`employee`
:   *string or null*

`check_in`
:   *string (RFC 3339 timestamp)*

`check_out`
:   *string (RFC 3339 timestamp) or null*

`running`
:   *boolean*

`worked_hours`
:   *number*

`worked_minutes`
:   *integer*

`before`
:   The record before the edit; null when the edit created it.

    *null or object (attendance.schema.json)*

## ENVIRONMENT

`ODOO_URL`
:   Odoo server URL; overrides url from the config files.

`ODOO_DATABASE`
:   Odoo database name; overrides database.

`ODOO_USERNAME`
:   Odoo login, usually an e-mail address; overrides username.

`ODOO_PASSWORD`
:   Odoo API key, used for XML-RPC. Despite the name, not the login password.

`ODOO_WEB_PASSWORD`
:   Odoo login password, used for the web session of clock in and clock out.

`ODOO_TOTP_SECRET`
:   TOTP secret (base32 or otpauth:// URL) for accounts with two-factor authentication.

`ODOO_OP_TIMEOUT`
:   Timeout of the 1Password call that resolves [op_secrets], a Go duration; default 5s.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_NO_OP`
:   If 1, true, yes or on, [op_secrets] is ignored and the 1Password CLI is never called.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND`
:   Backend, odoo (default) or fake; --backend overrides it.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_FAKE_STATE`
:   State file of the fake backend; default odoo-work-cli-fake-state.json in the temporary directory.

`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
:   Base directory of the global config file; default ~/.config.

## FILES

`~/.config/odoo-work-cli/config.toml`
:   Global configuration ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/odoo-work-cli/config.toml if XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set). Created by odoo-work-cli config install.

`.odoo-work-cli.toml`
:   Configuration of a directory tree. Every such file from the filesystem root down to the current directory is merged over the global file, the deepest last. --config FILE loads only FILE instead.

`$TMPDIR/odoo-work-cli-fake-state.json`
:   State of the fake backend (--backend fake); ODOO_WORK_CLI_FAKE_STATE sets another path. Delete it to start over with the seed data.

## EXIT STATUS

0 on success, 1 on any error, including usage errors. With --json or --format json|jsonl the error is printed on standard output as one JSON object, {"error": {"kind": KIND, "message": TEXT}}, and nothing on standard error; otherwise as "Error: TEXT" on standard error, after usage errors followed by the usage.

Error kinds this command can fail with:

`auth`
:   Authentication failed: wrong API key or login password, TOTP rejected.

`access_denied`
:   Odoo's access rules forbid the operation, e.g. attendance writes without the Attendance Officer right.

`not_found`
:   The record does not exist or is not visible.

`validation`
:   Invalid input: unknown flag, bad argument, malformed date, time or hours, a time in the future, an unknown project.

`conflict`
:   The request contradicts the current state, e.g. clock in while clocked in, or an overlapping attendance record.

`network`
:   Odoo cannot be reached: DNS, connection refused, timeout, TLS.

`config`
:   The local configuration is missing or invalid.

`secrets_locked`
:   1Password is locked or unreachable, so op:// references could not be resolved.

`internal`
:   Anything else: an unexpected Odoo response or a bug.

## EXAMPLES

Correct the check-in of a day with one record:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli clock edit --date 2026-04-07 --in 08:00
Updated attendance #4605
  was: 2026-04-07 08:10 - 16:40 (8:30)
  now: 2026-04-07 08:00 - 16:40 (8:40)
```

A day with several records needs --id:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli clock edit --date 2026-04-08 --id 4607 --out 17:30
Updated attendance #4607
  was: 2026-04-08 12:30 - 17:00 (4:30)
  now: 2026-04-08 12:30 - 17:30 (5:00)
```

Backfill a day, but never overwrite an existing record:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli clock edit --date 2026-04-06 --in 09:00 --out 13:00 --create-only
Created attendance #5000: 2026-04-06 09:00 - 13:00
```
